title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous page). A^•_• is a simplicial object in cochain complexes. A^i_n is the group of i-forms on the n-simplex, as in Sullivan's polynomial forms or, in this manuscript, divided-power polynomial forms over Z. M is a coefficient group and C^•_{•M} is the simplicial complex of M-valued cochains on the standard simplices. A family k_n : A^n_n → M ('integration over Δ_n') satisfying the Stokes condition k_n∘∂_{n+1} = k_{n+1}∘d, with ∂_{n+1} = Σ(-1)^i d_i, is exactly a morphism of simplicial cochain complexes A → C_M.

The de Rham map. For a simplicial set X_•, global forms are Γ(X, A^n_X) = Hom_{sSet}(X, A^n_•). The page makes the induced map u : Γ(X, A_X) → C^•(X, M) explicit: send f : X → A^n_• to its degree-n component f_n : X_n → A^n_n, and set u^n(f) = k_n∘f_n ∈ Hom(X_n, M) = C^n(X, M). Grothendieck says this map, coming from the 'Stokes–De Rham morphisms' (k_n), realises the canonical map Γ(X, A_X) → RΓ(X, A_X). When A is a resolution of M (previous page), the target is ≅ RΓ(X, M) ≅ C^•(X, M). So the page sets up an abstract de Rham theorem for simplicial sets.

Existence and uniqueness of integration maps. Assume:
- (a) A^i_n = 0 for i > n; it suffices that d(A^n_n) = 0 for n ≥ 1.
- (b) H^n(A^•_n) = 0 for n ≥ 1.
- (c) H^{n-1}(A^•_n) = 0 for n ≥ 2.
Then a Stokes system (k_n) exists and is determined by k_0. The next page adds that a given k_0 extends iff k_0∘∂_1 kills Ker(d : A^0_1 → A^1_1).

Proof (implicit, it checks). By (a) and (b) every ω ∈ A^{n+1}_{n+1} is exact, ω = dη, so one must put k_{n+1}(dη) = k_n(∂η); hence uniqueness. This is well defined iff k_n∘∂ vanishes on closed elements of A^n_{n+1}. For n ≥ 1, (c) makes such η exact, η = dξ, and then k_n(∂dξ) = k_n(d∂ξ) = k_{n-1}(∂∂ξ) = 0. For n = 0 one needs exactly the next-page condition.

The next page notes the resulting morphism lands in normalised (non-degenerate) cochains. It also introduces a 'universal' de Rham complex with values in A_0/∂_1(Ker d), and an augmentation variant c') H^0(A^•_1) ≅ ε^*A^0_0. The whole serves the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex: an integral analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham theorem.
errors: No mathematical error. The inductive argument is only implicit ('on sait'), but it checks, and the n=0 condition is supplied on the next page.
Terminology wavers: the transcription reads 'complexe simplicial' with an insertion '{+cosimplicial[?]+}'. Formally A^• is simplicial in the lower index, as needed for Hom(X_•, A^n_•) to make sense.

ideas.what: Integration maps k_n : A^n_n → M satisfying Stokes are the same as a morphism of simplicial cochain complexes A → C_M. Through Hom(X, A^n_•), this gives a de Rham map Γ(X, A_X) → C^•(X, M) for any simplicial set X, realising Γ → RΓ.
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial (PL) de Rham theorem; Sullivan's integration map A_PL → C^*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), Dupont (1976), Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976), H. Cartan (1976 'Théories cohomologiques')

ideas.what: Axioms (a) vanishing above degree n, (b) and (c) vanishing of top and sub-top cohomology of A_n, under which a Stokes system exists and is uniquely determined by k_0. Plus an explicit criterion for k_0 to extend (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness and existence of integration from Poincaré-lemma-type axioms on a simplicial cdga / cochain-complex object
ideas.usually_credited_to: Close in spirit to the 'extendable + Poincaré lemma' axiomatics of Cartan and Bousfield–Gugenheim / Félix–Halperin–Thomas. The precise top-degree uniqueness criterion is not standard as stated.

ideas.what: Application to divided-power polynomial forms on simplices to get an integral de Rham theorem (the lecture's theme).
ideas.modern_name: Integral / divided-power simplicial de Rham complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cenkl–Porter (tame homotopy, early 1980s) and later integral-model work; unsure of a definitive attribution

missed.claim: A minimal axiomatic criterion for a simplicial cochain complex to carry unique 'integration' maps to cochains. Only top-degree conditions are used: A^i_n = 0 for i>n, H^n(A_n) = 0, H^{n-1}(A_n) = 0. Integration is uniquely determined by k_0, with an explicit obstruction ∂_1(Ker d) at level 1. This is weaker and more economical than the usual 'Poincaré lemma in all degrees' hypotheses.
missed.quote: a) A^i_n = 0 si i > n ... b) H^n(A^•_n) = 0 si n ≥ 1  c) H^{n-1}(A^•_n) = 0 si n ≥ 2  Alors on sait qu'il y a un syst. k_n : A^n_n → M satisfaisant la condition de Stokes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean uniqueness statement for integration maps on integral or divided-power models of cochains. That is relevant to current work on integral and p-adic models of homotopy types and to comparison maps in prismatic or crystalline settings. The statement is elementary, though, and may be folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but essentially standard abstract simplicial de Rham theorem, contemporaneous with Sullivan, Cartan, Dupont and Bousfield–Gugenheim. The economical top-degree axioms and the uniqueness-from-k_0 remark are a nice unpublished detail but not deep.
transcription_corrections: 'qui dérive des morph.[?] de Stokes-De Rham' — reads plausibly as 'déduite des morph. de Stokes–De Rham'.
The inserted words over 'complexe' read 'cosimplicial' or possibly 'semi-simplicial'; uncertain.
Margin note on a) reads roughly '(il suffit A^n_n = Z^n_n, i.e. d(A^n_n)=0 si n≥1)', consistent with the transcription.
'Hom(X_•, A^*)' under the first arrow corresponds to the '‖' annotation in the image, i.e. Γ(X, A^*_X) = Hom(X, A^*).
